critical_insights.description: Separate external consistency/serial order from preserving specified application invariants; different guarantees can explain apparent disagreement.
TrueTime exposes bounded uncertainty; timestamp selection and waiting are not elimination of replication/transaction coordination.
Calvin moves agreement ahead of execution and deterministic locking reduces contention footprint; it does not make network agreement free.
Recognize Calvin transaction planning/read-write-set and nondeterminism requirements; include their cost when extrapolating to the proposed service.
Coordination-free correctness is conditional on invariant confluence for the specified operations, merge and invariants; not a universal claim for transfers or stock decrements.
Do not equate throughput, tail latency and partition-time availability; Calvin explicitly distinguishes its availability usage from CAP availability.
critical_insights.evidence: Calvin page 1 footnote 1 and section 6; other papers' evaluation sections

critical_insights.description: A discriminating experiment holds workload, resources and required guarantee fixed while varying contention, cross-partition ratio, network latency and relevant mechanism assumptions; measure correctness as well as performance.
critical_insights.evidence: Comparative experimental design requirement; no direct three-way comparison is supplied

critical_insights.description: Make the unresolved issue concrete: which service invariants and transaction classes can avoid coordination, and when remaining coordination becomes the bottleneck; ground a conditional hybrid rather than claiming an already-proven universal winner.
critical_insights.evidence: Synthesis from the three papers; explicitly a task-level inference

catastrophic_risks.description: Treating bounded clock uncertainty as perfect clocks or assuming TrueTime alone replaces agreement.
Allowing arbitrary stock decrements/transfers to merge without validating relevant invariants, causing oversell or conservation failures.
Claiming the papers directly prove a universal performance winner or equivalent guarantees under every partition/workload.
catastrophic_risks.evidence: Different system models and experimental conditions; Calvin page 1 footnote 1

competing_solutions: Coordinate all relevant multi-record operations under a sufficiently strong transaction guarantee, accepting its cost.
Use deterministic preordering for known transaction footprints and explicitly account for sequencing, planning and replication costs.
Partition transaction classes by proven invariant-confluence conditions, coordinating only classes that need it; validate hybrid boundary semantics.
high_value_insights: Distinguish moving coordination outside lock-holding intervals from removing the semantic need for coordination.
Use a correctness-matched factorial microbenchmark to distinguish contention-footprint effects from weaker-guarantee effects.
success_criteria: Explains the apparent conflict without inventing contradictory experimental results or equating unlike correctness guarantees.
Grounds at least two mechanisms in accurate paper claims and clearly labels the service-specific hidden assumption and inference.
Proposes a feasible experiment with competing predictions, safety oracle, controls and a falsification outcome; no catastrophic unsafe claim.
